title: Pricing change notice and revenue reconciliation procedure (2025)
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:
This procedure sets out the cross-functional steps for changing pricing or billing terms for Redwood Inference customers, along with the revenue recognition (RevRec) and forecasting adjustments that follow. It aims to: (1) make legal and procurement approvals consistent; (2) give customers and internal teams predictable notice timelines; (3) produce auditable RevRec adjustments and journal entries; and (4) keep FP&A forecasts and committed capacity accounting current.

Scope:
- Covers any change to customer-facing pricing, billing cadence or contracted charge quantities: rate card changes, discounts, credits, one-time fees, term amendments, capacity commits and early termination fees.
- Excluded: marketing price lists that leave existing contracts unchanged, and internal list-price experiments (<72 hours) with no customer impact.

Key definitions:
- Pricing Change: any change to monetary terms in an executed agreement or active billing relationship.
- Amendment Effective Date: when the new pricing/billing terms legally take effect.
- Billing Cutoff Date: the last invoice date at the old pricing.
- RevRec Adjustment Window: 60 days post-amendment for accounting adjustments and catch-up.

Owners and responsibilities:
- Sales: raises the pricing change request and writes the commercial justification.
- Legal: drafts the amendment and approves final language.
- Procurement (customer side): confirms customer acceptance and PO alignment where needed.
- Finance (Revenue Operations / RevRec): confirms accounting treatment, prepares journal entries, issues billing adjustments.
- FP&A: updates forecasts and model assumptions.
- Billing/Payments (Finance Ops): issues invoices/credit memos and updates the billing system.
- Customer Success: explains operational impact and coordinates acceptance with the customer.

Notice triggers and SLAs:
1) Internal approval target: commercial, legal and finance approval must be in place 15 business days before Amendment Effective Date.
2) Customer-facing notice: standard notice is 45 days prior to Amendment Effective Date for recurring price increases or structural changes.
3) Expedited changes: with Executive sponsor approval the approval window can drop to 3 business days; Finance must manually check the RevRec impact before go-live.

Pre-change checklist (Sales lead):
- Confirm SKU mapping for affected charges.
- Provide the expected billing delta per customer (monthly run rate).
- State whether committed capacity or reserved billing is affected.
- Attach the customer PO or acceptance email where required.
- Choose the Amendment Effective Date and propose a Billing Cutoff Date.

Approval workflow:
1) Sales files a Pricing Change Request (PCR) in the Contract Intake Workspace (Confluence template) with customer, contract id, old/new rates, effective dates, reason, revenue owner and estimated MRR/ARR impact.
2) Legal reviews the draft amendment and flags non-standard clauses.
3) Finance (RevRec) determines accounting treatment and flags any revenue deferral or acceleration.
4) Procurement or Customer Success collects the customer's signature or PO.
5) Final sign-off is recorded in the PCR and the amendment is executed.

Billing execution and RevRec after the effective date:
1) Billing/Payments runs invoices at the new rates on or after the Billing Cutoff Date, applying the billing system's proration rules.
2) RevRec determines revenue impact by identifying any overlap where the old rate was recognized but the new rate applies.
3) For retrospective corrections (retro credits or back-billed invoices) Finance must a) prepare credit memos or invoices, b) record the journal entries, and c) document the rationale in the PCR.

Accounting treatment guidance:
- Prospective recurring price increase: recognize on the normal schedule and adjust future forecasts; no retrospective RevRec entry.
- Mid-term rate change with customer-approved back-billing: recognize the additional revenue when invoiced; if payment lands after period end, book a receivable and assess collectibility. Refer to ASC 606 contract modification guidance.
- One-time credits or refunds: issue a credit memo and reduce recognized revenue within the RevRec Adjustment Window, linking the credit memo to the amendment id.

Sample journal entries (illustrative):
- Prospective increase: no change to historical entries.
- Retro billing for Jul-Sep, invoiced in October:
  Debit: Accounts Receivable $30,000
  Credit: Revenue (prior periods catch-up) $28,000
  Credit: Deferred Tax/Other adjustments $2,000  (if tax or timing)
- Credit for overbilling:
  Debit: Revenue Reduction/Contra-Revenue $5,000
  Credit: Accounts Receivable or Cash $5,000

Forecasting & FP&A alignment:
- FP&A must update recurring revenue models within 10 business days of amendment execution, covering monthly run-rate, churn adjustments, committed capacity revenue schedules and the GAAP vs. cash waterfall.
- Material amendments (>5% of ARR per customer or >$250k ARR delta) need a reconciliation memo from FP&A and RevOps, presented at the next Finance weekly forecast review.

Reconciliation controls (monthly):
- Revenue Operations produces the Pricing Change Reconciliation report (PCRR) listing executed amendments, effective dates, invoiced deltas, open credit memos and pending disputes.
- Example pseudo-query:
  SELECT contract_id, amendment_id, effective_date, sum(new_amount - old_amount) as monthly_delta
  FROM billing_events
  WHERE effective_date BETWEEN :start_date AND :end_date
  GROUP BY contract_id, amendment_id

- Revenue Ops keeps a mapping table of amendment ids to invoice ids for the reconciliation scripts; exceptions open a ticket for RevRec manual review.

Customer communication template (condensed):
- Subject: "Notice: Updates to your Redwood Inference pricing effective [DATE]"
- Include: short rationale, affected SKUs, Amendment Effective Date, Billing Cutoff Date, a contact, the amendment link and PO update instructions.

Escalation matrix:
- Day 0-5 after amendment: Billing/Payments handles invoicing and simple disputes.
- Day 6-30: RevRec and Sales resolve pricing discrepancies and approve credit memos.
- >30 days: escalate to the Head of Finance and General Counsel for disputes outside the standard Credit Policy window.

Controls and evidence retention:
- Every pricing change lives in the Contract Intake Workspace with links to the executed amendment PDF, PCR ticket, customer acceptance and invoice/credit memo ids.
- Evidence is retained for 7 years for audit.

Templates and artifacts:
- PCR Confluence template: [link to template]
- Amendment checklist: 1) commercial summary, 2) legal clause exceptions, 3) RevRec sign-off, 4) invoices to reissue, 5) communications log.
- Sample credit memo JSON:
  {
    "customer_id": "CUST-12345",
    "amendment_id": "AMEND-2025-011",
    "amount": "-5000.00",
    "currency": "USD",
    "reason_code": "PRICE_CORRECT"
  }

Operational notes:
- When a pricing change alters committed capacity, work with Infrastructure Finance to update GPU reservation invoicing and capacity reporting.
- Apply rounding and proration consistently: per-day proration for mid-cycle changes unless the customer asks otherwise.
- Prefer prospective amendments where possible to avoid retroactive accounting and disputes.

KPIs:
- Time-to-approval (goal: <15 business days)
- Share of pricing changes needing retrospective correction (goal: <5%)
- Average time to clear pricing disputes (goal: <15 business days)
- Forecast delta accuracy after pricing changes (goal: <2% variance vs. revised forecast)

Appendix A - Example calculation:
- Customer A paid $100k monthly at the old rate. On 2025-12-01 the rate rose to $110k monthly. Amendment Effective Date: 2025-12-01. Billing Cutoff Date: 2025-12-01.
  - Prospective only: the December invoice shows $110k; nothing historical changes.
  - If November is back-billed at the new rate with customer approval: an extra invoice for the $10k November delta.
